title: Console Walkthrough - Usage Analytics & Per-Route Cost Breakdown
summary: Redwood AE + SE ran a console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for retail inference pipelines; top concerns: cost per-conversation, latency SLOs, and multi-tenant data isolation. Agreed next steps: send detailed pricing, share sample per-route dashboard export, schedule POC kickoff and security docs.
action_items: Maya Chen (Redwood): Send detailed pricing matrix + example cost spreadsheet - due 2026-02-18
Theo Alvarez (Redwood SE): Export a sample per-route dashboard and share JSON/CSV - due 2026-02-17
Rachel Park (Nova Retail): Share current traffic distribution by route and p95 latency targets - due 2026-02-20
Samir Patel (Nova Retail): Provide security contact for SOC2 and VPC questions - due 2026-02-18
next_steps: Redwood to share pricing, per-route dashboard export, and security docs
Schedule POC kickoff with engineering (aim for 2026-02-22 to 2026-02-26 window)
Customer to send traffic sample and success criteria (cost/latency)
transcript: [00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. We'll do a quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics and the per-route cost breakdown Theo will hop in for the demo.
[00:18] Rachel: Hi Maya, thanks — Rachel here. We're particularly interested in seeing cost attribution per route. We have chat & summarization routes and want to know where the spend is happening.
[00:30] Theo: Awesome. Quick logistics — I might share my screen. If at any point you want to jump to a specific route, just call it out.
[00:45] Samir: Sounds good. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated. Latency is big for checkout chat flows; cost is big for batch summarization jobs.

[01:05] Theo: Fair. Starting on the Console home: you can see aggregate usage by token, request count, and cost over time. Note that cost here is normalized to your pricing tier — in hosted mode we show actual billed tokens, in dedicated we show estimated cost with reserved capacity offsets.
[01:40] Rachel: I see. That "estimated cost" line — is that based on model per-token plus infra overhead? Sometimes model names get munged in exports, I've seen that before.

[01:55] Theo: Yeah, good question. It's a combination: model unit cost + amortized GPU infra for dedicated. Small transcription note — sometimes the export labels 'kv cache' as 'k v cache' in older CSVs, we've fixed most but you might see odd names if you pull older data.
[02:20] Maya: The important part is per-route tagging. If you tag requests at the API level — route:chat, route:summary — the console surfaces those as first-class filters and cost buckets.
[02:40] Aisha: Do we need to change our client instrumentation to include route tags? We currently just send a single service token.
[02:55] Theo: Minimal change: include a 'route' header or param. We support automatic mapping through SDKs and have a middleware example in the docs. We'll share the snippet after the call.
[03:20] Rachel: Can you show per-route p95 and cost per 1k requests? That's what the product team asks for.

[03:35] Theo: Yep. Switching to the per-route dashboard — here's route list on the left, select 'checkout-chat'. The top panel shows traffic, tokens, p50/p95 latencies, and an estimated cost-per-1k metric. The math is explained in the tooltip — token counts * model rate + batch/infra adjustments.
[04:05] Samir: That p95 spikes in the afternoon look like they're correlated with larger seq lengths. Can we break down by sequence bucket?

[04:20] Theo: You can. There's a 'sequence length' histogram; you can filter the chart to buckets (0-128, 128-512, 512+). That helps with quantization recommendations as well — big wins if most of your traffic is under 512.
[04:45] Rachel: Is there a way to see the actual requests that caused errors or falls back to a cheaper model variant? We had silent fallbacks in our tests last week.

[05:00] Theo: Yes — the tracing pane ties request IDs to fallback policy triggers. If a request hit a fallback (e.g., model not available -> smaller quantized variant), you'll see an event and the downstream cost difference. We can pull a sample for your traffic.
[05:25] Aisha: On the dedicated commit side, how do burst credits and autoscale impact the per-token cost math? We have big peaks during promo events.

[05:40] Maya: For Dedicated, your committed monthly cost covers baseline GPU pools. Bursts are charged extra; the console shows committed vs burst usage and attributes burst spend separately. You can apply routing policies to prefer dedicated for latency-critical routes and hosted for cheaper batch routes.
[06:05] Rachel: That routing feature — can we set percentage-based routing (e.g., 80% to dedicated, 20% hosted) as an experiment? We want to A/B cost vs latency.

[06:20] Theo: Yes, rollout rules support weighted routing. You can define route-level policies with weights, time windows, and health fallbacks. The console will simulate projected cost under that weighting too.
[06:45] Samir: Any caveats with KMS/HSM keys for Private deployments? Our security team will ask for audit log linkage.

[07:00] Maya: Private supports customer-managed KMS and we integrate audit logs with your SIEM. We'll send our SOC 2 docs and the private deployment checklist; I noted action to share security contact.
[07:20] Rachel: Great. Can you export a per-route cost CSV that we can feed into our finance model? Preferably with daily granularity for the last 90 days.

[07:35] Theo: Absolutely — there's an export button. I'll export a sample now for the last 30 days so you can see the schema: route, date, tokens_in, tokens_out, requests, p50_ms, p95_ms, estimated_cost_usd.
[07:55] [screen share pause / file prepping noise]

[08:10] Theo: Uploaded sample to the chat — link: /redwood/exports/novaretail-sample-per-route.csv (note: placeholder link, we'll email the real file). Some columns may have model alias mangling but the route field is reliable.
[08:35] Aisha: We run nightly summarization jobs that are long seq lengths; is there a recommended approach to reduce cost? Should we use a quantized model or batch differently?

[08:50] Theo: Two levers: model choice (quantized vs fp16) and batching. In Optimize we recommend batching windows for offline jobs to maximize GPU utilization; for online chat we prefer caching prefix tokens and smaller batch sizes to meet latency SLOs.
[09:10] Rachel: Can the console call out regression alerts if a new model push increases token consumption per response?

[09:25] Jordan: Yes — you can configure quality monitoring tied to prompt sets. If average tokens per response or perplexity rises beyond thresholds, the system can alert and even auto-rollback to a pinned model.
[09:45] Samir: That auto-rollback — is it only for hosted or works in private too?
[09:55] Theo: It works across environments; in Private the control plane can be run in customer-managed mode but the rollback logic is the same if you opt in to the control features.
[10:15] Rachel: We're also worried about attribution accuracy. If a single request touches multiple internal services, how do you ensure correct route attribution?

[10:30] Maya: Best practice: have the initiating service attach the 'route' tag and propagate it downstream. If propagation is broken, we fall back to the API token mapping which is coarse-grained. We'll share the middleware snippet and a diag tool to detect missing propagation.
[10:55] Aisha: Any documentation for the SDKs and examples? Our stack is node + go.
[11:05] Theo: Yes — we have SDK examples for node and go; they include route tagging middleware and a small shim to attach correlation IDs. I'll put links in the follow-up.
[11:25] Rachel: Let's talk pricing — are there volume bands visible in the console? We want to forecast at 50M tokens/month.

[11:40] Maya: Console shows a projected monthly bill based on current rates. For larger commits we recommend Dedicated reserved capacity — we'll run numbers for your 50M tokens and show a dedicated commit vs hosted comparison.
[11:58] Samir: If we do dedicated, how long are commits, and can we adjust model mix mid-commit?
[12:10] Maya: Commits are typically monthly or annual. You can adjust model mix; cost allocation will be rebalanced in the console. We'll provide an example amortization sheet.
[12:30] Rachel: Could you also show the anomaly detection for cost spikes? We had an unexpected run that doubled our spend one week in November.
[12:45] Theo: The anomaly view flags day-over-day or week-over-week deviations and ties them to route and model. You can drill in to see request IDs and whether a fallback or retry occurred.
[13:05] [brief cross talk]
[13:20] Rachel: One more ask — when you simulate weighted routing, does the console give a confidence band on projected latency? We don't want to overfit to averages.
[13:35] Jordan: It does — projections include median and 90% confidence intervals based on historical performance and sequence length distributions.
[13:50] Aisha: On exports, what's the max retention window? Our finance team needs 1 year of daily granularity.

[14:05] Maya: Hosted exports support 13 months retention on analytics; for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention or ship logs to your storage. We'll include the retention policy in the docs pack.
[14:25] Rachel: Okay, this is helpful. Can we review a sample per-route CSV now?
[14:35] Theo: Sure — quick walkthrough of the sample: here's checkout-chat with date, requests 12,345, tokens_in 1.2M, tokens_out 1.3M, p95 210ms, estimated_cost 432 USD for the day.
[14:55] Samir: That estimated_cost seems high; is the model listed as 'gpt-like-8k' or an internal alias? Sometimes aliases double-count tokens if both input/output are tallied incorrectly.

[15:10] Theo: We do both input and output tokens; the CSV includes both columns. If you prefer cost-per-output-token only, you can select that export flavor. Good catch on aliasing — we'll ensure aliases are normalized in the sample.
[15:30] Rachel: Can we get a quick demo of setting up a policy to route summarization to a quantized model and chat to a higher-SLA model?

[15:45] Theo: Yep — in the routing policies page create a new rule: match route:summary -> target model: redwood-quant-2 — weight 100. For checkout-chat match route:checkout-chat -> target model: redwood-bf16-low-latency, prefer dedicated pool.
[16:10] Rachel: And the console will show projected cost delta if we switch both today?
[16:20] Theo: It will show an instantaneous projection plus 7/30 day rolling projection. Again, it's based on your historical sequence distribution.
[16:40] Aisha: If rollback is triggered, do we get a Slack alert or email?
[16:50] Jordan: Both; integrations are via webhooks, PagerDuty, Slack. You can configure channels per project.
[17:05] Rachel: Ok, last items — we want a POC that validates cost savings on nightly summarization and maintains p95 < 300ms for checkout-chat. Can Redwood run a pilot on a slice of traffic?
[17:25] Maya: Yes. Typical pilot: 2 week POC, we run on 10-25% of traffic for checkout-chat and full night for summarization. We'll instrument dashboards and hand over exportable reports.
[17:45] Samir: Timeline expectation — we need security review clearance before spinning up dedicated or private. How long does that usually take?
[17:58] Maya: Security review typically 1-2 weeks depending on diligence items; we'll fast-track SOC2 docs and the private deployment checklist.
[18:15] Rachel: Great. Anything we missed?
[18:22] Theo: I noted to share: pricing sheet, per-route export sample, SDK middleware snippet, SOC2 and private deployment checklist. I'll attach the files in the follow-up email.
[18:35] Maya: Recap: Redwood sends pricing + dashboard export + security docs; Nova Retail sends traffic sample and target SLOs; schedule POC kickoff. Thanks everyone.
[18:50] Rachel: Thanks, Maya and team. Talk soon.
[19:00] [meeting end]
